evidence: "Floyd-Warshall"; "full = (1 << t) - 1"; "dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(1 << t)]"
affordance_in_statement: This synchronization is fully transitive: any group of towers connected together by a sequence of active links will merge their data into a single, identical shared database. You are free to activate links involving non-priority towers; while they do not originate any logs, they will successfully synchronize and pool any data they receive.
secondary_shortcut_name: small terminal subset enabling bitmask dynamic programming
removal_suggestion: Do not state the connectivity-to-common-database equivalence or explicitly describe non-priority towers as relays. Present synchronization operationally as logs being propagated by the activation protocol, with the same feasible outcomes, so the Steiner-tree reduction is not handed to the solver in one sentence.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Reduces the network to shortest-path distances and uses terminal-subset optimization, exploiting relay towers as Steiner vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Fully transitive synchronization through sequences of active links, including links through non-priority towers.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a terminal bitmask DP over states of size 2^t, the standard Steiner-tree formulation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The complete set of logs is pooled by any connected group, so one connected subgraph can serve all priority towers.

common_affordance: The explicit equivalence between a connected activated subgraph containing all priority outposts and complete log synchronization, with non-priority towers usable as Steiner relay vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Treats the task as an ordinary minimum spanning tree or terminal-connection problem and does not correctly account for a shared non-priority Steiner structure that can connect several terminals more cheaply.

Computes shortest paths from priority towers and appears to combine them through a terminal metric/MST-style construction, which can double-count shared relay edges and is not sufficient for the minimum Steiner tree.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit transitivity and relay-tower explanation with an indirect operational description of the synchronization protocol, while preserving the same feasible activated-link sets and outcomes. In particular, avoid saying that every connected group merges into one database and that non-priority towers pool received data.
regression_risk: The edit could make the already-defeated qwen3-coder or glm-5 infer the intended Steiner-tree structure and accidentally correct their terminal-MST mistakes.
